title: Validate and correlate the webview message protocol
description:
Treat every message crossing the webview boundary as untrusted. The host currently accepts `any`, performs unchecked field access and persistence, silently ignores unknown types, and has no request correlation; declared protocol variants also lack handlers.

Define discriminated inbound/outbound message types with runtime type guards and bounded payload validation. Every operation receives an `operationId`; executions also receive an `executionId`. Responses, progress, acknowledgements, and errors must echo the relevant ID. Maintain an execution registry so cancellation targets one request, duplicate submission is controlled, and an older response cannot overwrite a newer request.

Validate messages in both directions, reject unknown enums and oversized/deep structures, and return stable error codes without leaking credentials or request bodies. Remove dead workspace protocol variants as part of the approved capability-gap deferral. No handler may persist, import, execute, or generate code before validation succeeds.

checklist.text: Inventory actual senders and handlers, then reconcile the TypeScript protocol with implemented supported behavior
Implement runtime validators for every inbound and outbound payload, enum, identifier, size, and nesting boundary
Add operationId and executionId correlation to requests, acknowledgements, progress, responses, cancellation, and errors
Maintain an execution registry and make cancellation target exactly one in-flight request
Prevent stale or out-of-order messages from mutating the active request, response, history, or loading state
Return structured protocol errors for unknown messages without logging secrets or untrusted bodies
Remove or explicitly deprecate dead workspace messages and add malformed/race/cancellation regression tests
